name: TX-36
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+12 partisan lean favors incumbent Brian Babin
Democrat Rhonda Hart has raised no money and shows no visible campaign infrastructure
Babin holds a roughly $911,000 war chest for his re-election bid
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at only about 4%
model.rationale: The race sits in a strongly Republican-leaning East Texas district where Babin is a well-funded incumbent, while Hart has reported no fundraising or cash on hand. With no independent polling and no expert ratings, the fundamentals and prediction markets all point to an easy Republican hold.
model.watch: Any sign of Democratic fundraising or outside spending in the district would be the first signal the race could tighten, though the structural lean makes an upset unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
TX-36 is a heavily Republican district in east Texas with a partisan lean of about twelve points toward the GOP. Brian Babin, the incumbent, is running for another term and has built a substantial campaign account of more than $900,000. His Democratic opponent, Rhonda Hart, has reported no fundraising and no cash on hand, indicating a campaign with limited resources.

There are no public polls of the race and no expert ratings to draw on, so the outlook rests on the district's fundamentals. Prediction markets give Democrats only a small chance of winning. All available evidence points to Babin being strongly favored to hold the seat, with the main open question being the size of his victory margin rather than the outcome itself.
